marks.gloss_en: on 17 Tammuz the tablets were broken
on 9 Av it was decreed on our fathers that they not enter the land
from when Av enters, joy is reduced
there were no days as joyous for Israel as 15 Av
and the daughters of Jerusalem go out and dance in the vineyards

and so it says 'go forth and see, daughters of Zion, King Solomon, with the crown his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding and on the day of the gladness of his heart' (Song 3:11): 'the day of his wedding' -- this is the giving of the Torah
תעניות ומעמדות מי איכא מוסף? -- fasts and maamadot have no musaf, so how can the priests lift their hands four times a day on them?
חסורי מיחסרא והכי קתני: on the three occasions they lift their hands at every prayer, and on some of them four times (= p_chasorei_mechasra)
fasts have no additional (musaf) prayer
למה נסמכה פרשת כהן מברך לפרשת נזיר? לומר: מה נזיר אסור ביין, אף כהן מברך אסור ביין
according to all, at any rate, a drunk is forbidden to raise his hands
מתקיף לה אבוה דרבי זירא, ואמרי לה אושעיא בר זבדא: אי מה נזיר אסור בחרצן — אף כהן מברך אסור בחרצן! -- the juxtaposition would carry over the nazirite's grape-pit prohibition too
אמר קרא: לשרתו ולברך בשמו -- the blessing priest is juxtaposed also to the ministering priest, who is permitted grape-pits (= m_hekesh_kohen_meshares)
לשרתו ולברך בשמו: מה משרת מותר בחרצן — אף כהן מברך מותר בחרצן
R' Yitzchak: just as the ministering priest is permitted grape-pits, so the priest who blesses is permitted grape-pits
דתניא... רבי יהודה אומר: שחרית ומוסף יש בהן נשיאת כפים, מנחה ונעילה אין בהן -- the baraita gives R' Yehuda exactly the Sages' position
R' Meir: mincha too has the raising of the hands
והאידנא מאי טעמא פרשי כהני ידייהו במנחתא דתעניתא? -- if the halakha is R' Yosei's (no blessing at mincha), why do priests nowadays bless at a fast's mincha?
כיון דבסמוך לשקיעת החמה קא פרשי — כתפילת נעילה דמיא (= p_samuch_lishkia_kneila)
והלכה כרבי יוסי -- the Gemara rules with Rav Nachman
Rav Nachman: the halakha follows R' Yosei
this [the mishnah's four times] is the statement of R' Meir
R' Meir (per the stam): every day the priests do not spread their hands at mincha because of drunkenness
R' Yehuda (per the stam): shacharit and musaf, where drunkenness is not common on every day -- the Rabbis did not decree about them
R' Yosei (per the stam): mincha, which exists every day -- the Rabbis decreed about it
Rav: the halakha follows R' Meir
the one who said 'halakha' means: we expound it in the public lecture
